source_ref: Buechel S & Hahn U (2017) EACL 2017 vol 2:578-585, aclanthology.org/E17-2092 ; full CrowdFlower instructions in Appendix A of the arXiv posting arXiv:2205.01996 (same paper) ; data deposit github.com/JULIELab/EmoBank (Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.7440748, corpus/individual_{writer,reader}_ratings.csv, corpus/README.md); IRW script data/emobank_buechel_2017.R
note: Items are the six rating scales of the EmoBank annotation task: 5-point SAM Pleasure/Arousal/Control, asked once from the author ('Expressing Emotion') and once from the reader ('Evoking Emotion') perspective. mapping_basis=data_labels: the IRW code IS the source column plus the source file, with data/emobank_buechel_2017.R doing only recode(V='valence', A='arousal', D='dominance') and pasting the file's perspective -- no positional assignment -- and corpus/README.md documents V/A/D as Valence/Arousal/Dominance. That tie was still checked against the data (all 30 item x resp cells match the deposit exactly; see verify script), because the resp DIRECTION was an inference. TEXT: item_text is the verbatim per-panel paragraph of the task instructions from Appendix A of arXiv:2205.01996, and section_prompt the verbatim Getting Started / Instructions / Hints / Final Note framing of that perspective's task. The two perspectives' framing differs in wording, so it is recorded per section_id and `instructions` is left blank rather than duplicating one of them. Source line breaks became single spaces; nothing else was normalised, including the source's own missing comma in the reader Pleasure panel ('people are happy, pleased satisfied, contented or hopeful') and the writer Control panel's 'Please take a moment' without the comma the other five panels carry. option_text is the SAM pole label printed in Figure 2 at resp=1 (Unhappy/Annoyed/Unsatisfied; Calm/Relaxed/Sleepy; Submissive/Influenced/Guided) and resp=5 (Happy/Pleased/Satisfied; Excited/Nervous/Aroused; Dominant/In control/Influential); the source prints no label at positions 2-4, which are left blank rather than padded. The pole-to-number direction was verified from the data (see verify script). RIGHTS: no non-commercial, fee or no-redistribution clause is quotable for this wording. The shipped text is Buechel & Hahn's own instruction prose, published by them in an openly licensed paper (ACL Anthology CC BY 4.0) beside a CC BY-SA 4.0 data deposit; it is adapted from Bradley & Lang (1999). Figure 2 carries the line 'Copyright of the original SAM by Peter J. Lang 1994', but that covers the manikin pictograms, which IRW does not ship -- only the authors' prose and the printed pole labels.
public_note: In this table `id` is an EmoBank sentence, not a person, and `item` is the rating scale (Pleasure/Arousal/Control) crossed with the annotation perspective (writer/reader), so the item text shown is the SAM scale prompt the crowdworker read, not the sentence being rated -- that stimulus text is keyed to `id` in the EmoBank deposit's corpus/raw.csv

source_ref: expfactory attention_network_task/experiment.js (MIT) as administered in the Self-Regulation Ontology battery; Enkavi et al. 2019 PNAS 116(12):5472-5477, doi:10.1073/pnas.1818430116; raw data github.com/IanEisenberg/Self_Regulation_Ontology Data/Complete_02-16-2019/Individual_Measures/attention_network_task.csv.gz
note: Cognitive task, not a questionnaire: each `item` is a trial-type (stimulus condition), built by data/enkavi_2019_conflict_tasks.py as cue_flankertype_middledirection_location -- a join of four of the source data file's own columns, so the code carries no positional or order inference. The words shipped come from the expfactory `attention_network_task` experiment source that this battery administered (github.com/expfactory/expfactory-experiments, MIT): `instructions` is the two instructions_block pages verbatim, with the HTML markup stripped and the entities rendered (← -> the left-arrow character, — -> em dash); nothing was added or paraphrased. `item_text` renders each condition's stimulus display in the study's OWN notation -- the instructions themselves write the arrays as arrow/dash strings ('e.g <-<-<-<-<-, or -- -- -> -- --') -- so it is a transcription of the source's representation, not an invented description; the cue clause names the cue display defined for that cue value in experiment.js (nocue = fixation only, center = * at fixation, double = * top and bottom, spatial = * at the target's location). The item-code-to-stimulus tie was checked directly against the study's released data file (Self_Regulation_Ontology/Data/Complete_02-16-2019/Individual_Measures/attention_network_task.csv.gz): over 75,168 test-stage rows each of the 48 item keys has exactly ONE distinct `stimulus` HTML value and exactly one `correct_response`, and all 48 decoded arrow arrays plus location match the shipped item_text character for character (0 mismatches). That is why mapping_basis is data_labels and Step 5b is exempt: the source data file itself ties code to stimulus, per row, with no inference for statistics to add. `correct_response` is source_published -- the raw file's `correct_response` column holds jsPsych keycodes 37/39, transcribed here as 'left arrow key' / 'right arrow key' (the instructions' own phrase 'the corresponding arrow key'). resp is trial ACCURACY (the source's boolean `correct`), so option_text is Incorrect/Correct, matching the practice-phase feedback strings in the task source; it is not the participant's keypress. section_prompt left blank and a single trivial section_id used -- the cue is a visual display belonging to the item, not a shared textual prompt. Rights: task source is MIT, the response data is CC BY by the authors' written confirmation (see the processing script header); no NC, fee or no-redistribution clause anywhere, so no wording_rights flag.
public_note: Item text for this cognitive task renders each trial's visual display -- the cue and the five-symbol arrow/dash array, in the task's own notation -- because the Attention Network Task presents images rather than written item wording; and resp is trial accuracy (1 = correct), not the key the participant pressed, so option_text reads Incorrect/Correct
